minutes.headline: Committee heard the FY19 school budget at a 3% increase with a hiring freeze, and sent the memorial policy back to subcommittee.
minutes.summary: The superintendent and business director presented the FY19 school budget as a level-service 3% budget going to Town Hall, with enrollment, Chapter 70 and circuit breaker context and a hiring freeze because of expected Title I losses. Record kindergarten registration forced a proposal for a fourth screening day. Residents protested removal of a memorial jersey from the field house, and the committee sent the memorial naming policy back to subcommittee rather than vote. Routine votes covered minutes, line-item transfers, a proclamation, an Italy trip, and an MASC contract.

budget_items.what_was_said: The initial request was a higher increase, but the committee voted the bottom line at the 3% level that fits the town manager's recommendation and goes to Town Hall.
Business director said the state-calculated per-pupil cost was below the state average.
Share of Chapter 70 funds used for the school budget has risen since FY14.
State reimbursed at a rate below full funding; the budget was built on the lower rate and no money is set aside for unanticipated placements.
Budget is a 3% increase; second year of a negotiated contract with major groups; personnel is level service.
Title I funding is expected to fall sharply after the census, prompting a hiring freeze; final numbers not known until summer.
The health insurance line, over a two million dollar item, drives the non-personnel increase.
Two-thirds of the ninth-grade Chromebook purchase comes from 40R housing money, which has dropped sharply.
Facilities director asked to move funds, mostly from natural gas, to building maintenance contract and supplies for elevator repair and an architect.

what_happened.line: The committee voted the FY19 school bottom line at a level-service increase that fits the town manager's recommendation, and it goes to Town Hall.
A hiring freeze continues, except the primary school principal and new psychologist positions, because Title I funding is expected to fall after the census.
The memorial naming policy third reading was not voted; it goes back to the policy subcommittee for public input after residents protested the removal of a memorial jersey.
The committee voted to authorize the chair to sign the MASC consultant contract for the superintendent search; printing the search brochures was rejected as too costly.
Initial approval of the 2019 Italy trip and a set of line-item transfers were voted, but the vote counts were not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: The budget going to Town Hall sets how much of the town budget, mostly taxes, goes to the schools, and the Title I freeze and lower 40R housing money mean staffing and Chromebook purchases may change once final figures arrive.
The memorial policy and the superintendent search are open: residents can give input at the policy subcommittee, and the search will shape who leads the district.
